description: Does a WCF client call work on Linux? Keyed by target framework, platform, binding (config element name), effective security mode and the credential type that mode uses ('None' when the mode is None; '*' matches any; the most specific entry wins). Verdicts: compatible, requires_change, incompatible, or unknown where nothing is established (unprobed); each that is not compatible says what must change and who changes it (we, backend_owner, or we_or_backend_owner). Same sourcing and confirmation flow as wcf-client-support: every entry names its sources, may carry probe results, and must be confirmed by a person before a report built on it goes to a client.

entries.basis: chart Linux: Kerberos/HTTP supported; release v2.0.0: Windows authentication on Http transport on Linux; release v1.0.0-rc2: Kerberos on Linux needs the OS's GSSAPI components
entries.caveat: Windows credentials negotiate Kerberos on Linux. On our side: a Kerberos client in the image (krb5 and GSSAPI), a krb5.conf for the domain, and credentials or a keytab for the calling identity. Otherwise the backend's owner offers a credential a Linux caller can present without the domain: a certificate, a username or a token. Which applies is decided by a probe in a Kerberos environment.

fix.change: Kerberos configuration on our side, or a credential change by the backend's owner

entries.basis: probe wsHttp-TransportWithMessageCredential-Certificate: the .NET 10 WCF client 8.1.2 on Linux throws System.UriFormatException ('Invalid URI: The format of the URI could not be determined.') while signing the message with the client certificate — XML canonicalization, XmlTextReaderImpl.ConvertAbsoluteUnixPathToAbsoluteUri via ExcCanonicalXml and SignedXml.ComputeSignature — before anything is sent. The same client binary passes on Windows against the same service. It fails alike with System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.12 and 8.0.10
entries.caveat: Established by probe; the chart has no WS-binding row. Message-level certificate signing on other HTTP bindings (basicHttp, ws2007Http, netHttp TransportWithMessageCredential/Certificate) takes the same path and is unprobed.

fix.change: the backend's owner must offer Linux callers another security mode or credential: message-level certificate signing fails in the .NET WCF client on Linux

revision.decision: reviewer decision: replaces net10.0/linux/wsHttpBinding/*/* (compatible in 1.0.0), which this probe contradicted

rules: A wildcard entry (a * for security mode or credential type) may not assert that a call works (platform: compatible; runtime: supported or supported_with_caveat) for a binding whose behaviour depends on its security mode or credential type — every binding in this matrix has one. Only a specific entry can. A wildcard may assert that a call does not work, or needs a change, or that it is unprobed (unknown). Enforced by a test over both matrices (SoapRuntimeVerdictTests).
